# Glossary: Core Concepts & Formulas {.unnumbered}

This glossary provides a comprehensive reference of the foundational definitions, mathematical formulas, and concepts introduced throughout the textbook and tested in SOCIOL 111 assessments.

---

## Introduction to Networks & Graph Theory {.unnumbered}
*Lessons 1–3*

### Network (Graph) {.unnumbered}

A formal mathematical representation composed of a set of discrete objects (nodes or vertices) and a collection of ties (edges) specifying connections between them.

**Formula / Metric:**

$$
G = (V, E)
$$

* **Primary Section:** [What are Networks?](https://olizardo.github.io/networks-textbook/lesson-theory-what-are-networks)
* **Assessment Context:** Homework 1 &bull; Quiz 1 (Lesson 1)

---

### Social Network {.unnumbered}

A network where the nodes represent social entities (individuals, organizations, nations) and the edges represent socially defined relationships (friendship, advice, communication, trade).

* **Primary Section:** [What is a Social Network?](https://olizardo.github.io/networks-textbook/lesson-theory-what-are-social-networks)
* **Assessment Context:** Homework 1 &bull; Quiz 1 (Lesson 1)

---

### Social Network Analysis (SNA) {.unnumbered}

The distinct sociological subfield combining relational theory, empirical measurement, graph theory, and matrix algebra to study patterned relations between social actors.

* **Primary Section:** [What are Networks?](https://olizardo.github.io/networks-textbook/lesson-theory-what-are-networks)
* **Assessment Context:** Homework 1 &bull; Quiz 1 (Lesson 1)

---

### Vertex / Node ($V$) {.unnumbered}

The fundamental unit or discrete actor in a network graph. The total number of vertices $|V|$ is the order of the graph ($N$).

**Formula / Metric:**

$$
N = |V|
$$

* **Primary Section:** [Introduction to Graphs](https://olizardo.github.io/networks-textbook/lesson-graphs-intro)
* **Assessment Context:** Homework 1 &bull; Quiz 1 (Lesson 2)

---

### Edge / Tie ($E$) {.unnumbered}

A link or connection between a pair of nodes. In an undirected graph, an edge is an unordered pair $\{i, j\}$; in a directed graph, it is an ordered pair $(i, j)$.

**Formula / Metric:**

$$
M = |E|
$$

* **Primary Section:** [Introduction to Graphs](https://olizardo.github.io/networks-textbook/lesson-graphs-intro)
* **Assessment Context:** Homework 1 &bull; Quiz 1 (Lesson 2)

---

### Node Degree ($k_i$) {.unnumbered}

The number of edges incident to (connected with) node $i$. In directed graphs, split into in-degree ($k_i^{in}$) and out-degree ($k_i^{out}$).

**Formula / Metric:**

$$
k_i = \sum_{j} A_{ij}
$$

* **Primary Section:** [Basic Graph Metrics](https://olizardo.github.io/networks-textbook/lesson-graphs-metrics)
* **Assessment Context:** Homework 1 &bull; Quiz 1 (Lesson 2)

---

### Node Neighborhood ($N(i)$) {.unnumbered}

The set of all nodes directly adjacent to node $i$. In directed graphs, distinguished as the in-neighborhood (senders to $i$) and out-neighborhood (receivers from $i$).

**Formula / Metric:**

$$
N(i) = \{j \in V : \{i, j\} \in E\}
$$

* **Primary Section:** [Introduction to Graphs](https://olizardo.github.io/networks-textbook/lesson-graphs-intro)
* **Assessment Context:** Homework 1 &bull; Quiz 1 (Lesson 2)

---

### Graph Density ($D$) {.unnumbered}

The proportion of possible edges that actually exist in the graph. Ranges from 0 (empty graph) to 1 (complete graph / clique).

**Formula / Metric:**

$$
D_{undirected} = \frac{2M}{N(N-1)}, \quad D_{directed} = \frac{M}{N(N-1)}
$$

* **Primary Section:** [Basic Graph Metrics](https://olizardo.github.io/networks-textbook/lesson-graphs-metrics)
* **Assessment Context:** Homework 1 &bull; Quiz 1 (Lesson 2)

---

### Dyad {.unnumbered}

A pair of nodes and the potential relations between them. In directed networks, classified into three mutually exclusive states: Mutual ($M$), Asymmetric ($A$), or Null ($N$).

**Formula / Metric:**

$$
Total dyads = \binom{N}{2} = \frac{N(N-1)}{2}
$$

* **Primary Section:** [Dyads and Triads](https://olizardo.github.io/networks-textbook/lesson-graphs-dyads-triads)
* **Assessment Context:** Homework 1 &bull; Quiz 1 (Lesson 3)

---

### Multiplexity {.unnumbered}

The coexistence of multiple distinct types of relational ties (e.g., friendship, co-working, advice) between the same pair of social actors.

* **Primary Section:** [Social Ties & Network Boundaries](https://olizardo.github.io/networks-textbook/lesson-theory-ties-bound)
* **Assessment Context:** Homework 1 &bull; Quiz 1 (Lesson 3)

---

### Triad Census (MAN Scheme) {.unnumbered}

A vector enumerating the frequencies of all 16 possible isomorphic directed configurations of three nodes, labeled by counts of Mutual ($M$), Asymmetric ($A$), and Null ($N$) dyads.

**Formula / Metric:**

$$
e.g., 003, 012, 102, 021D, 021U, 021C, 111D, 111U, 201, 030T, 030C, 120D, 120U, 120C, 210, 300
$$

* **Primary Section:** [Dyads and Triads](https://olizardo.github.io/networks-textbook/lesson-graphs-dyads-triads)
* **Assessment Context:** Homework 1 &bull; Quiz 1 (Lesson 3)

---

## Matrices, Paths & Connectivity {.unnumbered}
*Lessons 4–5 & 7*

### Adjacency Matrix ($A$) {.unnumbered}

A square $N \times N$ matrix representing a network of $N$ nodes, where $A_{ij} = 1$ if an edge directs from node $i$ to node $j$, and $0$ otherwise. For undirected networks, $A$ is symmetric ($A = A^T$).

**Formula / Metric:**

$$
A_{ij} \in \{0, 1\}, \quad A_{ii} = 0 \text{ (no self-loops)}
$$

* **Primary Section:** [The Adjacency Matrix](https://olizardo.github.io/networks-textbook/lesson-matrix-network)
* **Assessment Context:** Homework 2 &bull; Quiz 2 (Lesson 4)

---

### Row & Column Sums {.unnumbered}

In a binary adjacency matrix, the sum across row $i$ gives the out-degree of node $i$, while the sum down column $j$ gives the in-degree of node $j$.

**Formula / Metric:**

$$
k_i^{out} = \sum_{j=1}^N A_{ij}, \quad k_j^{in} = \sum_{i=1}^N A_{ij}
$$

* **Primary Section:** [Matrix Operations: Row & Column Sums](https://olizardo.github.io/networks-textbook/lesson-matrix-operations)
* **Assessment Context:** Homework 2 &bull; Quiz 2 (Lesson 4)

---

### Walk, Trail, and Path {.unnumbered}

A walk is any alternating sequence of nodes and edges. A trail is a walk with no repeated edges. A path is a walk with no repeated nodes.

**Formula / Metric:**

$$
Length = number of edges traversed
$$

* **Primary Section:** [Indirect Connections & Paths](https://olizardo.github.io/networks-textbook/lesson-graphs-paths)
* **Assessment Context:** Homework 2 &bull; Quiz 2 (Lesson 5)

---

### Geodesic Distance ($d_{ij}$) {.unnumbered}

The length of the shortest path connecting node $i$ and node $j$. If no path exists, $d_{ij} = \infty$.

**Formula / Metric:**

$$
d_{ij} = \min(\text{path length from } i \text{ to } j)
$$

* **Primary Section:** [Indirect Connections & Paths](https://olizardo.github.io/networks-textbook/lesson-graphs-paths)
* **Assessment Context:** Homework 2 &bull; Quiz 2 (Lesson 5)

---

### Connected Component {.unnumbered}

A maximal subgraph in which every pair of nodes can reach one another via a path. In directed graphs, distinguished as strongly connected (path in both directions) or weakly connected (path ignoring edge directions).

* **Primary Section:** [Graph Connectivity](https://olizardo.github.io/networks-textbook/lesson-graphs-connectivity)
* **Assessment Context:** Homework 2 &bull; Quiz 2 (Lesson 5)

---

### Tree Graph & Spanning Tree {.unnumbered}

A connected acyclic graph. A tree of $N$ nodes always has exactly $N - 1$ edges. A spanning tree is a subgraph that includes all $N$ vertices of $G$ with minimum edges ($N-1$).

**Formula / Metric:**

$$
M_{tree} = N - 1
$$

* **Primary Section:** [Tree Graphs](https://olizardo.github.io/networks-textbook/lesson-graphs-trees)
* **Assessment Context:** Homework 2 &bull; Quiz 2 (Lesson 5)

---

### Powers of the Adjacency Matrix ($A^k$) {.unnumbered}

The entry in row $i$, column $j$ of $A^k$ equals the exact number of walks of length $k$ starting at node $i$ and ending at node $j$.

**Formula / Metric:**

$$
[A^k]_{ij} = \text{number of walks of length } k \text{ from } i \text{ to } j
$$

* **Primary Section:** [Matrix Multiplication](https://olizardo.github.io/networks-textbook/lesson-matrix-multiplication)
* **Assessment Context:** Homework 3 &bull; Quiz 2 (Lesson 7)

---

### Matrix Transpose ($A^T$) {.unnumbered}

The operation of flipping a matrix across its diagonal ($[A^T]_{ij} = A_{ji}$). In directed networks, $(A^T)$ reverses the direction of every edge.

**Formula / Metric:**

$$
[A^T]_{ij} = A_{ji}
$$

* **Primary Section:** [Basic Matrix Operations](https://olizardo.github.io/networks-textbook/lesson-matrix-operations)
* **Assessment Context:** Homework 3 &bull; Quiz 2 (Lesson 7)

---

## Ego Network Layers & The Strength of Weak Ties {.unnumbered}
*Lesson 6*

### Strength of Weak Ties (SWT) {.unnumbered}

Granovetter's thesis that weak ties act as bridges between socially distant clusters, transmitting novel, non-redundant information (such as job opportunities), whereas strong ties foster local redundancy and emotional support.

* **Primary Section:** [The Strength of Weak Ties](https://olizardo.github.io/networks-textbook/lesson-theory-swt)
* **Assessment Context:** Homework 3 &bull; Quiz 2 (Lesson 6)

---

### Forbidden Triad {.unnumbered}

Granovetter's assumption that if actor $A$ has strong ties to both $B$ and $C$, the dyad between $B$ and $C$ cannot remain null—they will inevitably form at least a weak tie due to time allocation and cognitive balance.

**Formula / Metric:**

$$
Strong A-B and Strong A-C \implies At least Weak B-C
$$

* **Primary Section:** [The Strength of Weak Ties](https://olizardo.github.io/networks-textbook/lesson-theory-swt)
* **Assessment Context:** Homework 3 &bull; Quiz 2 (Lesson 6)

---

### Dunbar's Circles {.unnumbered}

A hierarchical, layered model of ego network capacity constrained by cognitive and temporal limits: Support Clique (~5), Sympathy Group (~15), Affinity Group (~50), and Active Social Network (~150).

**Formula / Metric:**

$$
Scaling ratio \approx 3\times per layer (5 \rightarrow 15 \rightarrow 50 \rightarrow 150)
$$

* **Primary Section:** [Dunbar's Theory of Social Circles](https://olizardo.github.io/networks-textbook/lesson-theory-dunbar)
* **Assessment Context:** Homework 3 &bull; Quiz 2 (Lesson 6)

---

## Affiliation Networks & Centrality {.unnumbered}
*Lessons 8–9*

### Affiliation / Two-Mode Network {.unnumbered}

A bipartite graph containing two distinct classes of nodes (e.g., people and events/organizations), where ties exist only between nodes of different classes, never within the same class.

**Formula / Metric:**

$$
Represented by rectangular incidence matrix B (N \times M)
$$

* **Primary Section:** [Affiliation Networks](https://olizardo.github.io/networks-textbook/lesson-sna-affiliation-networks)
* **Assessment Context:** Homework 4 &bull; Quiz 3 (Lesson 8)

---

### One-Mode Projection {.unnumbered}

Deriving single-mode networks from an affiliation matrix $B$: $P = B B^T$ produces person-by-person shared memberships; $E = B^T B$ produces event-by-event overlapping attendees.

**Formula / Metric:**

$$
P = B B^T \quad (N \times N), \quad E = B^T B \quad (M \times M)
$$

* **Primary Section:** [Affiliation Networks](https://olizardo.github.io/networks-textbook/lesson-sna-affiliation-networks)
* **Assessment Context:** Homework 4 &bull; Quiz 3 (Lesson 8)

---

### Duality of Persons and Groups {.unnumbered}

Breiger's sociological formulation that social actors are structurally defined and connected by their joint group affiliations, while social groups are defined by their overlapping memberships.

* **Primary Section:** [Affiliation Networks](https://olizardo.github.io/networks-textbook/lesson-sna-affiliation-networks)
* **Assessment Context:** Homework 4 &bull; Quiz 3 (Lesson 8)

---

### Degree Centrality ($C_D$) {.unnumbered}

A local measure of prominence based directly on the number of adjacent neighbors. Standardized by dividing by the maximum possible degree ($N-1$).

**Formula / Metric:**

$$
C_D(i) = \frac{k_i}{N - 1}
$$

* **Primary Section:** [Degree Centrality](https://olizardo.github.io/networks-textbook/lesson-sna-degree-centrality)
* **Assessment Context:** Homework 4 &bull; Quiz 3 (Lesson 9)

---

### Closeness Centrality ($C_C$) {.unnumbered}

A global metric reflecting how close an actor is to all other nodes in the network, calculated as the inverse of the sum of geodesic distances from node $i$ to all others.

**Formula / Metric:**

$$
C_C(i) = \frac{N - 1}{\sum_{j \neq i} d_{ij}}
$$

* **Primary Section:** [Closeness Centrality](https://olizardo.github.io/networks-textbook/lesson-sna-closeness)
* **Assessment Context:** Homework 4 &bull; Quiz 3 (Lesson 9)

---

### Betweenness Centrality ($C_B$) {.unnumbered}

A metric measuring the degree to which an actor falls on the shortest paths between all other pairs of nodes, quantifying positional gatekeeping and potential control over information flow.

**Formula / Metric:**

$$
C_B(i) = \sum_{j < k, j \neq i \neq k} \frac{\sigma_{jk}(i)}{\sigma_{jk}}
$$

* **Primary Section:** [Betweenness Centrality](https://olizardo.github.io/networks-textbook/lesson-sna-betweenness)
* **Assessment Context:** Homework 4 &bull; Quiz 3 (Lesson 9)

---

### Eigenvector Centrality ($C_E$) {.unnumbered}

A recursive centrality measure where an actor's importance is proportional to the sum of the centralities of the actors to whom they are connected (being connected to well-connected alters).

**Formula / Metric:**

$$
\lambda C_E(i) = \sum_{j} A_{ij} C_E(j) \implies A v = \lambda v
$$

* **Primary Section:** [The Big Three Centralities](https://olizardo.github.io/networks-textbook/lesson-sna-bigthree)
* **Assessment Context:** Homework 4 &bull; Quiz 3 (Lesson 9)

---

## Brokerage & Structural Holes {.unnumbered}
*Lessons 10–11*

### Structural Hole {.unnumbered}

A buffer or separation between two actors or groups who possess non-redundant resources and are not directly connected. Burt's theory states that bridging structural holes yields competitive advantages, autonomy, and good ideas.

* **Primary Section:** [Structural Holes and Brokerage](https://olizardo.github.io/networks-textbook/lesson-theory-sht)
* **Assessment Context:** Homework 5 &bull; Quiz 3 (Lesson 10)

---

### Gould & Fernandez Brokerage Typology {.unnumbered}

Five distinct tripartite brokerage roles based on group membership of the source ($A$), broker ($B$), and target ($C$): Coordinator ($A=B=C$), Consultant ($A=C \neq B$), Gatekeeper ($A \neq B=C$), Representative ($A=B \neq C$), and Liaison ($A \neq B \neq C$).

**Formula / Metric:**

$$
5 Roles: Coordinator, Consultant, Gatekeeper, Representative, Liaison
$$

* **Primary Section:** [Structural Holes and Brokerage](https://olizardo.github.io/networks-textbook/lesson-theory-sht)
* **Assessment Context:** Homework 5 &bull; Quiz 3 (Lesson 10)

---

### Homophily ('Birds of a Feather') {.unnumbered}

The principle that similarity breeds connection: individuals form ties with socially similar alters at higher rates than with dissimilar alters. Split into choice homophily (preference) and baseline/induced homophily (opportunity structure).

* **Primary Section:** [Theories of Ego Network Homogeneity & Diversity](https://olizardo.github.io/networks-textbook/lesson-theory-ego-homo)
* **Assessment Context:** Homework 5 &bull; Quiz 3 (Lesson 11)

---

### Feld's Focus Theory {.unnumbered}

Feld's structural explanation that social ties form around shared extra-network foci of activity (workplaces, voluntary clubs, classrooms), which organize joint interaction and generate induced homophily.

* **Primary Section:** [Theories of Ego Network Homogeneity & Diversity](https://olizardo.github.io/networks-textbook/lesson-theory-ego-homo)
* **Assessment Context:** Homework 5 &bull; Quiz 3 (Lesson 11)

---

## Ego Network Metrics & Data Collection {.unnumbered}
*Lessons 12–13*

### Effective Size {.unnumbered}

Burt's measure of an ego network's non-redundant size: ego's degree minus the average degree of alters with respect to other alters in the ego network.

**Formula / Metric:**

$$
ES_i = \sum_j (1 - \sum_q p_{iq} m_{jq})
$$

* **Primary Section:** [Ego-Network Metrics](https://olizardo.github.io/networks-textbook/lesson-sna-ego-networks)
* **Assessment Context:** Homework 6 &bull; Quiz 3 (Lesson 12)

---

### Blau Index of Diversity {.unnumbered}

A quantitative index measuring categorical heterogeneity in an ego network or group, ranging from 0 (complete homogeneity) to $(k-1)/k$ (equal distribution across $k$ categories).

**Formula / Metric:**

$$
B = 1 - \sum_{i=1}^k p_i^2
$$

* **Primary Section:** [Ego-Network Metrics](https://olizardo.github.io/networks-textbook/lesson-sna-ego-networks)
* **Assessment Context:** Homework 6 &bull; Quiz 3 (Lesson 12)

---

### E-I Index (Krackhardt & Stern) {.unnumbered}

An index measuring whether ties cross group boundaries: external ties minus internal ties divided by total ties. Ranges from $-1$ (all internal ties / complete homophily) to $+1$ (all external ties / complete heterophily).

**Formula / Metric:**

$$
EI = \frac{E - I}{E + I}
$$

* **Primary Section:** [Ego-Network Metrics](https://olizardo.github.io/networks-textbook/lesson-sna-ego-networks)
* **Assessment Context:** Homework 6 &bull; Quiz 3 (Lesson 12)

---

### Name Generator & Interpreter {.unnumbered}

The standard survey technique for ego network data. A name generator asks respondent (ego) to list alters meeting specific criteria; name interpreters then elicit demographic and relational attributes of each alter.

* **Primary Section:** [Collecting Ego-Network Data](https://olizardo.github.io/networks-textbook/lesson-sna-ego-collect)
* **Assessment Context:** Homework 6 &bull; Quiz 3 (Lesson 13)

---

### Position Generator {.unnumbered}

Lin's instrument to measure social capital by asking respondents whether they know someone in a standardized grid of structural occupations differing in occupational prestige.

* **Primary Section:** [Collecting Ego-Network Data](https://olizardo.github.io/networks-textbook/lesson-sna-ego-collect)
* **Assessment Context:** Homework 6 &bull; Quiz 3 (Lesson 13)

---

## Balance, Signed Graphs & Dominance Hierarchies {.unnumbered}
*Lessons 14–15*

### Signed Graph {.unnumbered}

A graph in which each edge is assigned a positive sign ($+$, representing liking, alliance, trust) or negative sign ($-$, representing disliking, hostility, distrust).

**Formula / Metric:**

$$
\sigma(e) \in \{+1, -1\}
$$

* **Primary Section:** [Dyadic & Triadic Balance](https://olizardo.github.io/networks-textbook/lesson-theory-balance-dyadic)
* **Assessment Context:** Homework 6 &bull; Quiz 4 (Lesson 14)

---

### Structural Balance Theorem {.unnumbered}

Harary & Cartwright's theorem proving that a signed graph is balanced if and only if its node set can be partitioned into two mutually hostile subsets such that all within-subset edges are positive and all between-subset edges are negative.

**Formula / Metric:**

$$
Triad is balanced \iff product of signs is positive: (+++) or (+--)
$$

* **Primary Section:** [Structural Balance](https://olizardo.github.io/networks-textbook/lesson-theory-balance-struct)
* **Assessment Context:** Homework 6 &bull; Quiz 4 (Lesson 14)

---

### Dominance Hierarchy (Tournament) {.unnumbered}

A complete, asymmetric directed network where between every pair of actors there is an unambiguous dominant-subordinate relation ($i \to j$ or $j \to i$, but never mutual or null).

**Formula / Metric:**

$$
M = \binom{N}{2} directed arcs with no mutual dyads
$$

* **Primary Section:** [Dominance Hierarchies](https://olizardo.github.io/networks-textbook/lesson-theory-hierarchies)
* **Assessment Context:** Homework 7 &bull; Quiz 4 (Lesson 15)

---

### Transitivity in Dominance {.unnumbered}

The structural condition where $i \to j$ and $j \to k$ implies $i \to k$. High transitivity creates a linear peck-order hierarchy; intransitive cycles ($i \to j \to k \to i$) produce instability.

**Formula / Metric:**

$$
i \to j \land j \to k \implies i \to k
$$

* **Primary Section:** [Dominance Hierarchies](https://olizardo.github.io/networks-textbook/lesson-theory-hierarchies)
* **Assessment Context:** Homework 7 &bull; Quiz 4 (Lesson 15)

---

## Subgroups & Positional Equivalence {.unnumbered}
*Lessons 16–17*

### Clique {.unnumbered}

A maximal complete subgraph of three or more nodes, in which every node is directly adjacent to every other node in the subgraph, and no other node in the network can be added without violating completeness.

**Formula / Metric:**

$$
Density within clique = 1.0
$$

* **Primary Section:** [Clique Analysis](https://olizardo.github.io/networks-textbook/lesson-sna-groups-cliques)
* **Assessment Context:** Homework 7 / 8 &bull; Quiz 4 (Lesson 16)

---

### Relaxed Subgroups ($n$-clique, $k$-plex) {.unnumbered}

Generalized cohesive subgroups: an $n$-clique allows maximum geodesic distance $\le n$ within the group; a $k$-plex allows each member to be disconnected from up to $k$ other group members.

**Formula / Metric:**

$$
n-clique: \max(d_{ij}) \le n; \quad k-plex: k_i \ge |S| - k
$$

* **Primary Section:** [Cohesive Subsets](https://olizardo.github.io/networks-textbook/lesson-sna-groups-cohesive)
* **Assessment Context:** Homework 7 / 8 &bull; Quiz 4 (Lesson 16)

---

### Core-Periphery Structure {.unnumbered}

A macroscopic network topology consisting of a densely connected inner core of actors and a sparsely connected outer periphery that connects to the core but not to each other.

* **Primary Section:** [Cohesive Subsets](https://olizardo.github.io/networks-textbook/lesson-sna-groups-cohesive)
* **Assessment Context:** Homework 8 &bull; Quiz 4 (Lesson 16)

---

### Structural Equivalence {.unnumbered}

Lorrain & White's mathematical definition: two nodes $i$ and $j$ are structurally equivalent if they have identical ties to and from all other nodes in the network ($A_{ik} = A_{jk}$ and $A_{ki} = A_{kj}$ for all $k \neq i,j$).

**Formula / Metric:**

$$
d_{E}(i, j) = \sqrt{\sum_{k} (A_{ik} - A_{jk})^2 + \sum_{k} (A_{ki} - A_{kj})^2} = 0
$$

* **Primary Section:** [Structural Equivalence & Similarity](https://olizardo.github.io/networks-textbook/lesson-theory-struct-equiv)
* **Assessment Context:** Homework 8 &bull; Quiz 5 (Lesson 17)

---

### Regular Equivalence {.unnumbered}

A generalized sociological role equivalence: actors $i$ and $j$ are regularly equivalent if they are connected to actors who are themselves regularly equivalent (e.g., all teachers connect to students, even if they have different students).

* **Primary Section:** [Structural Equivalence & Similarity](https://olizardo.github.io/networks-textbook/lesson-theory-struct-equiv)
* **Assessment Context:** Homework 8 &bull; Quiz 5 (Lesson 17)

---

### Blockmodeling {.unnumbered}

An analytic technique that partitions network nodes into discrete positional classes (clusters) and simplifies the network into an image matrix showing tie densities between positions.

**Formula / Metric:**

$$
Image Matrix \Delta where \Delta_{AB} \in \{0, 1\}
$$

* **Primary Section:** [Structural Equivalence & Similarity](https://olizardo.github.io/networks-textbook/lesson-theory-struct-equiv)
* **Assessment Context:** Homework 8 &bull; Quiz 5 (Lesson 17)

---

## Diffusion of Innovations & Dynamics {.unnumbered}
*Lesson 18*

### Diffusion of Innovations {.unnumbered}

The process by which an innovation (idea, practice, technology, disease) spreads through social network channels over time, characteristically producing an S-shaped cumulative adoption curve.

**Formula / Metric:**

$$
Logistic Curve: S(t) = \frac{1}{1 + e^{-a(t - t_0)}}
$$

* **Primary Section:** [The Diffusion of Innovations](https://olizardo.github.io/networks-textbook/lesson-theory-diffusion)
* **Assessment Context:** Homework 9 &bull; Quiz 5 (Lesson 18)

---

### Threshold Model (Granovetter) {.unnumbered}

A collective behavior model where an actor adopts a behavior only when the proportion (or absolute count) of their network alters who have already adopted exceeds the actor's individual adoption threshold.

**Formula / Metric:**

$$
Adopt if \frac{\sum_{j \in N(i)} y_j}{k_i} \ge \tau_i
$$

* **Primary Section:** [The Diffusion of Innovations](https://olizardo.github.io/networks-textbook/lesson-theory-diffusion)
* **Assessment Context:** Homework 9 &bull; Quiz 5 (Lesson 18)

---

### Small World Network {.unnumbered}

A network architecture (Watts & Strogatz) combining high local clustering (like a regular lattice) with short average geodesic path lengths (like a random graph), facilitated by occasional long-range shortcut ties.

**Formula / Metric:**

$$
L \sim \ln(N), \quad C \gg C_{random}
$$

* **Primary Section:** [The Small World Problem](https://olizardo.github.io/networks-textbook/lesson-theory-small-world)
* **Assessment Context:** Homework 9 &bull; Quiz 5 (Lesson 18)

---
